definition: In this learning context, ECM is a theoretical model used to explain why students continue choosing esthetic education courses. It links continued selection intentions to expectation confirmation and satisfaction, which affect persistence indirectly alongside other factors in the integrated analysis.

reasons: The packet does not define what “ECM” stands for or explicitly describe ECM as “a theoretical model used to explain why students continue choosing esthetic education courses.” It only states that the framework integrates “ECM and TPB” and studies intentions/behaviors regarding continued selection.

While the packet reports that “expectation confirmation and satisfaction … indirectly influence sustained selection intentions,” it does not explicitly state that this linkage is specifically due to ECM (as opposed to the integrated ECM+TPB framework).

The definition’s phrasing that ECM “links continued selection intentions to expectation confirmation and satisfaction” is not directly supported as an ECM-specific claim in the packet; the packet supports the existence of those variables’ indirect influence within an integrated analysis, not the claimed ECM mechanism.
